title: Soft-anchored capacity allocator for geo-failover routing
creator: Mateo Alvarez
description:
Purpose: implement a soft-anchored capacity allocator that combines latency-first routing with per-region capacity credits and probabilistic spillover to preserve SLOs during partial region degradation or failover events. The allocator should: (1) prefer geo-pinned endpoints when latency and credits permit; (2) gradually shift traffic away from an impacted region using a probabilistic hedging factor rather than an all-or-nothing cutover; (3) enforce circuit-breaker style backpressure and per-customer soft quotas to avoid overload on receiving regions; and (4) expose observability and controls in Console for operators to tune hedging fraction, credit refill rates, and emergency evacuation overrides.

Why: full hard failover leads to large tail spikes and cross-region overload (thundering herd) when an upstream region becomes degraded. A soft, capacity-aware approach reduces tail latency regression and provides smoother operator control during incidents.

Non-goals: this ticket does not change model variants or on-host batching logic; it focuses on request-level routing decisions and accompanying telemetry. On-prem private deployments will receive a compatible config surface but not the managed default rollout in this sprint.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Feature flagged allocator deployed to staging and canary.
2) Under controlled region degradation test (simulated 30% capacity drop), canary shows <10% increase in 99th pct tail compared to baseline and receiving regions remain within their configured SLA credit margins.
3) Console shows per-customer capacity-credit ledger and live hedging percentage.
4) Operators can atomically toggle emergency evacuation to full failover.
5) Unit and integration tests cover circuit-breaker tripping, credit accounting, and probabilistic routing outcomes.
6) Documentation and runbook published and linked in ticket.
design_notes:
Key components: credit ledger (per-region, per-customer), hedging function (input: latency delta, credit fraction, recent failure-rate; output: spill probability), admission controller that checks credit & circuit-breaker state, and telemetry hooks for SLO delta and credit burn rate. Trade-offs: probabilistic spill reduces atomicity of failovers (some requests still hit degraded region) but avoids overload spikes; credit granularity (per-customer vs per-tenant) impacts memory and bookkeeping—we start with per-customer for high-impact users and fall back to bucketed groups for others.

Kernel interactions: routing decisions are implemented in steering layer before request batching; ensure decision latency is <200us p50 to avoid toll on short tail requests. Use a small in-memory cache for credits with periodic persistence to the regional control plane store.

Circuit-breaker policy: open when capacity usage > 90% and error-rate > predefined threshold for 60s window; half-open probes allowed at 5% of prior traffic to validate recovery.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flagged implementation merged behind 'soft_anchored_allocator' flag.
2) Canary: route 1% of production traffic in us-east to allocator for 48h. Monitor 99p latency, credit burn, and inter-region egress.
3) Gradual ramp to 10% and then 25% with automated rollback triggers on (a) 99p latency > baseline + 15%, (b) receiving region credit utilization > 85% for >5m, or (c) spike in 5xx > 2x baseline.
4) Post-ramp: enable Console controls for SRE to tune hedging fraction and emergency evacuation.
5) After 2 weeks, promote to runtime-1.24 release and document config defaults.
telemetry: Expose metrics: allocator.hedge_probability{region,customer}, allocator.credit_balance{region,customer}, allocator.credit_burn_rate{region}, allocator.inter_region_spill{from_region,to_region}, allocator.circuit_state{region}, allocator.decision_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99). Link to dashboards: https://console.redwood/dashboards/allocator-hedge. Add SLO delta alerts: alert if estimated SLO regression > 5% for >10m.
test_plan: Unit tests for hedging math, credit accounting, and circuit-breaker transitions. Integration tests simulate region failure modes and assert graceful traffic shift behaviour. Load test with region capacity throttling to validate no receiving region exceeds configured credits. Chaos test: induce flapping in backbone to ensure stabilization hysteresis works. E2E canary validation pipeline: gate on telemetry thresholds and smoke tests of Console controls.
